players.product: OlympusMAX dry / adiabatic coolers and Marley Everest cooling towers for data-center heat rejection

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 results: total revenue grew 17.4% year-over-year (acquisitions plus organic growth in both segments); adjusted EBITDA increased 23% and adjusted EPS grew 22% to $1.69. HVAC segment revenue grew 22% with 11.5% inorganic growth and 9.6% organic growth (both cooling and heating); HVAC segment margin decreased 40 basis points, largely due to startup costs associated with the capacity expansions.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue +17.4%; adj. EPS $1.69 (+22%); HVAC revenue +22% (organic 9.6%); HVAC margin -40 basis points

quarterly_data.signal: HVAC segment backlog at Q1 quarter end was $755 million, up 38% organically year-over-year, primarily driven by data center demand; management said bookings are 'a little bit ahead' of where it expected and it sees opportunities going into backlog for 2026 plus opportunities to be executed in 2027.

2026 data center growth outlook raised from roughly 50% to 70%, driven by large customers pushing for accelerated deliveries; SPX pulled levers and added new lines to expand capacity, predominantly in its Olathe and Springfield facilities, and Olathe came online earlier than anticipated. CEO framed data center revenue as $200 million last year and in the $350 million neighborhood this year; rest of HVAC growing mid-single digits. Management called data center demand 'very strong' and 'accelerating', with attractive runway into 2027 and 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 data center growth 50% to 70%; ~$350 million in 2026 vs $200 million last year

quarterly_data.signal: Data center capacity plan (as of Q1): the capacity expansions give SPX the ability to serve circa $550 million of data center revenue, incremental off a $200 million base (about $400 million more capacity vs this year's ~$350 million, with possible further levers). Olathe should reach full capacity around mid-2027; the TAMCO Tennessee facility full capacity in 2027; Madison, Alabama does assembly only in the back half of 2026, full production capacity in the first half of 2027, and full capacity in the middle of 2028. Sites are built flexibly to run whichever product line is most needed.
quarterly_data.figure: data center revenue capacity circa $550 million (incremental off a 200 base; about $400 million more capacity); Olathe full capacity mid-2027; Madison full capacity middle of 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Production milestones in Q1 2026: SPX began production of the Marley OlympusMAX in its Olathe, Kansas facility and began producing highly engineered aluminum dampers in TAMCO's new Tennessee facility (3 lines up, adding a fourth, already shipping). Madison, Alabama build-out is well underway, with assembly capabilities for Marley OlympusMAX and custom air handling in the second half of 2026 and initial production in the first half of 2027. Startup costs for the expansions are about $8 million-$9 million, with 2/3 landing in Q1 and Q2; management said that, peeling out those startup costs, Q1 would show roughly 40 basis points of year-over-year margin lift.
quarterly_data.figure: OlympusMAX production began in Olathe in Q1; TAMCO Tennessee 3 lines up; startup costs $8 million-$9 million

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 guidance raised: adjusted EPS guidance increased by $0.15 to a midpoint of $7.95, reflecting strong Q1 results and additional data center-related volume to be delivered in the second half; guidance implies 21% adjusted EBITDA growth at the midpoint. It includes a $0.05-$0.10 headwind from Section 232 tariff changes (about $10 million gross cost, ~50% offset mainly through price), predominantly hitting HVAC in Q2 via Canadian businesses; no tariff impact expected on 2027 earnings. Custom air handling (Ingenia) production is moving into the US via the Madison facility.
quarterly_data.figure: adj. EPS guidance +$0.15 to $7.95 midpoint; 21% adj. EBITDA growth; tariff impact $0.05-$0.10

quarterly_data.signal: Data center customer mix and product demand: SPX serves a number of hyperscalers and colos plus chip manufacturers; existing large customers 'want more' and there are new hyperscaler and colo customers, with demand described as broad-based and the hyperscalers' increased CapEx seen 'front and center'. CEO said SPX is the global leader in cooling towers for data centers, TAMCO holds a strong position in actuated dampers and air movement, and much of the growth is in dry and adiabatic cooling, a newer area where some customers are buying for the first time; GW-scale sites want custom engineering, modularity and power/water efficiency (PUE/WUE).

Supply chain for data center products: management reported no supply chain delays; SPX designs its own proprietary fans, gearboxes, motors and heat exchange, and runs a rigorous supply check before taking more purchase orders. Rapid growth has put 'a little pressure' on it and it has added some new suppliers, while working to secure supply for continued growth in 2027 and 2028.

Semiconductor fab cooling: after softness in battery and semiconductor markets, SPX sees early bidding, including one project it believes it is very well positioned to win (names under confidentiality); SPX is typically strong with a lot of the largest semiconductor OEMs, some of which specify SPX as the choice for cooling towers, though management does not expect a return to the level of a couple of years ago.
